theory.intro: A **hemisphere** is half a sphere, so its curved surface is $2\pi r^{2}$, half of $4\pi r^{2}$. What else you add depends on the solid: an **open** hemisphere is a hollow bowl, a **closed** one also has a flat circular face.
facts: The curved surface of any hemisphere is $2\pi r^{2}$ — half of a sphere's $4\pi r^{2}$.
To find a hemisphere's surface area, decide whether it is **open or closed**, find the radius and calculate the area using the matching formula.
When a **diameter** is given, halve it to get $r$ before substituting.
Keep the working exact and round only on the last line; area is in **square** units.
steps: Decide whether the hemisphere is open or closed.
Write the matching formula: open $2\pi r^{2}$, closed $3\pi r^{2}$.
Substitute the radius, halving a diameter first, then evaluate.

workedExamples.solution_text:
The bowl has only a curved surface, so take half the surface area of a sphere.

$\begin{aligned} A &= \frac{1}{2}\times4\pi r^{2} \\ &= 2\pi(5.5)^{2} \\ &= 60.5\pi \\ &\approx 190.07\,\mathrm{cm}^{2} \end{aligned}$

Halve the diameter to find the radius.

$r=\frac{13}{2}=6.5\,\mathrm{cm}$

The open bowl has no flat circular face.

$\begin{aligned} A &= \frac{1}{2}\times4\pi r^{2} \\ &= 2\pi(6.5)^{2} \\ &= 84.5\pi \\ &\approx 265.46\,\mathrm{cm}^{2} \end{aligned}$

foundation.question_text:

development.question_text:
An open hemispherical bowl has a radius of $4.5\text{ cm}$ and no flat face.
Find its surface area, correct to $2$ decimal places.
development.solution_text:
An open hemisphere uses $2\pi r^{2}$.
$A = 2\pi r^{2}$
$= 2\pi(4.5)^{2}$
$= 40.5\pi$
$= 127.2345\ldots$
$\approx 127.23\text{ cm}^{2}$

development.question_text:
A hemispherical mixing bowl is open at the top (it has no flat face) and has a diameter of $24$ cm.
Find the area of its curved surface, correct to $2$ decimal places.

An open hemisphere has a radius of $6.5\text{ cm}$ and no flat face.
Find its surface area, correct to $2$ decimal places.

An open hemispherical bowl has a radius of $2.5\text{ cm}$ and no flat face.
Find its surface area, correct to $2$ decimal places.
development.solution_text:
An open hemisphere uses $2\pi r^{2}$.
$A = 2\pi r^{2}$
$= 2\pi(2.5)^{2}$
$= 12.5\pi$
$= 39.2699\ldots$
$\approx 39.27\text{ cm}^{2}$

mastery.question_text:
An open hemispherical dome has a radius of $8.5\text{ m}$ and no flat face.
Find its surface area, correct to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
Only the curved surface is included, so use $2\pi r^{2}$.
$A = 2\pi r^{2}$
$= 2\pi(8.5)^{2}$
$= 144.5\pi$
$= 453.9601\ldots$
$\approx 453.96\text{ m}^{2}$

practice.coverageNote: The booklet teaches both open and closed hemisphere formulas, but its standalone hemisphere calculations ask for open-hemisphere surface area from a radius or diameter. Practice and quiz items adapt Path Foundation question 2(a–c), using harder values in Development and Mastery and rounding final answers to 2 decimal places.
